text: The first NUDT15 (MTH2) crystal structure reveals it prefers nucleotide substrates other than 8-oxo-dGTP; structural features explain its differing substrate preferences versus MTH1. Depleting NUDT15 did not affect 8-oxo-dGTP incorporation into DNA or cancer cell survival in the tested lines. NUDT17 and NUDT18 were also profiled, showing far less activity than MTH1 against oxidized nucleotides. Conclusion: NUDT15 is not a biologically relevant 8-oxo-dGTPase; MTH1 remains the most prominent known sanitizer of the cellular dNTP pool. Context: deregulated redox metabolism in cancer causes oxidative dNTP damage, making dNTP pool sanitizing enzymes such as MTH1 promising anticancer targets.
